notes: The +14% pass-rate delta comes almost entirely from TWO evals. nuxt-nats: with-skill 5/5 vs baseline 1/5 — the baseline cannot know the proprietary module API (defineNatsConsumer, jsPublish, NatsEvents, NUXT_NATS_WORKERS). dlq: with-skill 5/5 vs baseline 4/5 — the baseline built the DLQ off deliveryCount and missed the MAX_DELIVERIES advisory.

The other 5 evals (architecture, deployment, operations, agent-fabric, feature-gating) scored 100% in BOTH configs. The assertions are keyword-level and the base model is strong on public NATS knowledge, so they do not discriminate. The skill's real added depth there (e.g. the feature-gating run's runtime api.level probe vs the baseline's static version check) is not visible in a keyword pass — judge those qualitatively in the Outputs tab.
Cost of the skill: roughly +59s wall-clock and +14k tokens per run on average (reading SKILL.md + reference files).
Grades are heuristic keyword/regex matches, not semantic. Treat them as a screen; the qualitative review is authoritative.

The runs surfaced a REAL skill bug, independently reported by 3 subagents and confirmed: the Go examples use the field name 'Backoff' where nats.go's ConsumerConfig is 'BackOff' (won't compile). Present in work-queue.md, go.md, consumers.md. One agent also flagged that nats.ErrMaxMessagesExceeded/ErrMaxBytesExceeded sentinels may not exist in current nats.go.
